function: Learned downlink transmit precoding (TPC matrix) for a LEO satellite UPA serving single-antenna users from delayed CSI, maximizing sum rate (pp. 1, 4-7).
system: LEO satellite, 3x3 UPA (M=9), K=2 single-antenna mobile users, TDD downlink at 2 GHz (5 GHz also tested), bandwidth 0.02f, Starlink-like constellation; no RIS (pp. 2, 8, 10).
method: DDPG actor-critic deep reinforcement learning with dense networks and state augmentation for delayed observations and rewards; trained online on a sum-rate reward (pp. 5-7, 9).
data_channel: Own MATLAB-simulated Rician LOS+NLOS satellite channel (Doppler, delay, UPA response) over a Starlink-like constellation above the Lake District, UK; 2,000,000 time steps, K=2 (pp. 4-5, 8-9).
test_conditions: Online learning curves; delays Td=0,1,16, pilot rates, handover thresholds 0-0.2 and 2 versus 5 GHz, each a separate curve; adaptation after handovers over 300 s (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: robust non-DL precoding [31]; learned: CNN channel prediction plus CNN beamforming [6], LSTM-based prediction [13] mapped by the authors' DRL precoder; perfect-CSI upper bound (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Average episodic sum rate (bit/s/Hz), reward, actor and critic losses, per-user rate, number of handovers (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Order of time complexity of actor and critic dense networks, O((Td+1) M^2 K^2) per time step for the method; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "We used Matlab for generating the satellite movements, selecting the satellite in service via Algorithm 1, and generating the CSI throughout time". Custom Rician LOS+NLOS model adopted from [13]-[15], [27] (p. 4) with random paths and Rician factor (p. 8); no 3GPP TR 38.811, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 1: "the DRL agent is capable of promptly adapting to the environment when a handover occurs". Figs. 3-5 (p. 10) track the online-learning agent's rate across handovers to new satellites; there is no frozen-model test, and the delay, pilot-rate and frequency cases are separate learning curves (borderline, see notes).
q3_support: p. 11: "We have chosen the works in [6], [13], [31] as a benchmark for our research". Fig. 6 compares the average rate with CNN prediction plus beamforming [6] and LSTM-based prediction [13] (learned) and with the non-DL method [31] (p. 12).
q4_support: p. 12: "the order of time complexity for our method is scaled by" O((Td+1)M^2K^2) per time step; the complexities of the actor and critic networks are also given.
q5_support: p. 9: "The output CSI was then used as a .mat matrix". The data are the authors' own simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and names no public dataset.
notes: Area 6 rather than 3: the learned precoder runs on a LEO satellite downlink and 6 precedes 3 in the specificity order; the 3x3 satellite array means the single-antenna check does not apply. The handover rule (Algorithm 1, p. 4) is a non-learned distance rule; only the precoder is learned. q2 is borderline: it rests on adaptation after handovers in online RL (abstract, Figs. 3-5), not on a frozen-model test, so the reviewer should confirm.
